title: Fifty Kilos of Metal
subtitle: 战争与和平 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 战争与和平（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）
meta: 主题语境：战争与和平（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）　|　核心词汇：bomb　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 bomb 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1943 my mother was sent to defuse ① a bomb she could not lift, and she said the lifting was the whole of the lesson. The ② bomb, meaning the device and not the explosion, was fifty kilos and was carried by whoever came last; a bomb, she said, is the only thing in a cellar that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ bomb in that crate had the same fuse, and the ④ bomb at the end, meaning the one the sergeant carried and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever counted properly. A bomb, my grandmother said, is nine parts metal and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the metal is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ bomb was the whole of the war, meaning the war it stood for and not the device. The ⑥ bomb, meaning the war and not any of that, is the only thing in a century that everybody fears and nobody questions; a bomb, he said, is either something you defuse or the only word that means both a device and a war. She said the war is the part they remember.

By 1965 the ⑦ bomb had become a photograph in a report, and the report had become an argument about the metal. The ⑧ bomb of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was fifty kilos of device and eleven years of lifting; a bomb, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ bomb I remember is the one at the end, which was drawn in 1971 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ bomb, my grandmother said in 1979, is the only thing that improves by being defused; every bomb, she said, is a war that has agreed to look like a device. She said the war was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 炸弹（指装置本身，与爆炸相对）
C. 固定搭配：defuse a bomb 拆除炸弹的引信
D. n. 炸弹（指箱里每一颗）
E. n. 炸弹（指末尾那一颗）
F. n. 炸弹（抽象：它所代表的那场战争）
G. n. 那场战争（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a bomb she could not lift
The bomb, meaning the device and not the explosion
bomb was the whole of the war
the bomb had become a photograph in a report
The bomb of the whole thing
A bomb, my grandmother said in 1979

answers.why: defuse a bomb 意为“拆除炸弹的引信”，1943 年母亲被派去拆一颗她抬不动的炸弹。
bomb 意为“炸弹”，指装置本身而不是爆炸，重五十公斤，由最后走的人搬走。
bomb 指箱里每一颗炸弹，每一颗都是同样的引信。
bomb 指末尾那一颗（中士搬的那一颗），是唯一有人认真清点过的。
bomb 意为“炸弹”，抽象指它所代表的那场战争，父亲说 bomb 就是那场战争的全部。
bomb 为抽象用法，指那场战争本身，是一个世纪里人人都害怕、却没人质疑的东西。
bomb 意为“炸弹”，到 1965 年这颗 bomb 成了报告里的一张照片。
bomb 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是五十公斤的装置与十一年的搬动。
bomb 意为“炸弹”，我记得的是末尾那一颗，1971 年被画下来，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
bomb 为抽象总称，祖母说炸弹是唯一会因为被引信拆除而变好的东西。
